tasks.title: Problem 1
tasks.statement: Photometry and radial velocity data for the Cepheid type star HV2257 are given in Table 1-3, based on observations by Gieren (MNRAS vol 265, 1993) . The pulsation period of the star is 𝑃 = 39.294 days. A reference graph for the temperature – color relation and the bolometric correction tables are given in Figure 1 (Houdashelt et al., 2000) and Table 4 (http://xoomer.virgilio.it/hrtrace/Straizys.htm). Given that the solar luminosity is 𝐿⨀ = 3.96 × 1026 𝐽 𝑠 −1 and its bolometric magnitude 𝑀⨀𝑏𝑜𝑙 = 4.72. Please do not use period-luminosity relation from the second question for this question.

parts.question: Calculate the average radial velocity of the star.
parts.reference:
Calculation of ΔR from the radial velocity graph (20 points)
For finding ΔR, we can use radial velocity curve, taking two moments, t1 and t2, between which the expansion acceleration can be assumed constant,
Δ𝑅 = (𝑣2 − 𝑣1) * (Δ𝜑 * 𝑃) / 2
So, from radial velocity curve we choose the part of the graph which is close to linear : t1 = 0.75, t2 = 0.85
Which corresponds to v(t1) = 272 km/s, v(t2) = 230 km/s
Now we can calculate Δ𝑅 = -7.13 * 10^9 m

parts.question: Calculate the distance to this pulsating star using the observed data and supplementary data given in Table 4 and Figure 1. Assume that there is no extinction in this direction.
parts.reference:
Solar absolute bolometric magnitude calculation (5 points): F⨀ = 3.31 * 10^-10 W/m^2
Formula derivation (15 points): R1 = ΔR / [ (T2/T1)^2 * 10^(-(m2-m1)/5) - 1 ]
Temperatures and magnitudes from photometric data (10 points): V1 = 13.58, V2 = 12.55, (V-R)1 = 0.81, (V-R)2 = 0.53, T1 = 4000K, T2 = 4750K, BC1 = -1.23, BC2 = -0.52, m_bol(t1) = 12.35, m_bol(t2) = 12.03
Calculate R1 (10 points): F1 = 2.584 * 10^-13 W/m^2, R1 = 4.0 * 10^10 m
Calculate distance (10 points): d = 9.72 kpc
Answer: 9.72 kpc

tasks.title: Problem 2
tasks.statement:
BVRIJHKLMN photometry of 2 stars from the constellation Cassiopeia is given in Table 5. For both stars it is believed that their light is affected by extinction by diffuse Interstellar Medium (ISM) only. Assuming that the observation is done from outside the atmosphere.

Now apply these results in order to derive a distance estimate for IC 342, a spiral galaxy in Cassiopeia obscured by Milky Way. You should assume that the properties of the ISM in IC 342 are similar to those of the ISM in our Galaxy.

parts.question: Using the data given in Tables 5 to 9, plot 𝐸X−V /𝐸B−V as a function of 1/𝜆X for filters B, V, R, I, J, H, K, L, M, N for both stars. Fit approximate curves by eye (in particular, note that 𝐸X−V / 𝐸B−V ~ 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡. as 1/𝜆X → 0). X is each band in the photometric system.
parts.reference: Using the data from tables 5 to 9 and recalling that MK class II corresponds to giant stars while MK classes Ia and Iab correspond to supergiants, we easily obtain tables 10 to 12 and hence figures containing the plots of E_{X-V}/E_{B-V} against 1/\lambda_X for both stars. (Tables 10-12 and plots: 30 points total)

parts.question:
Using the graphs obtained in a), estimate 𝑅V for each star.
𝑅V = 𝐴V / 𝐸B−V
(𝐴V is the absorption in V, and 𝐸B−V is the color excess)
parts.reference:
We have that E_{\lambda-V} = A_{\lambda} - A_V \rightarrow -A_V as \lambda \rightarrow \infty, so the plot of E_{X-V}/E_{B-V} against 1/\lambda_X intersects the vertical axis at -A_V / E_{B-V} = -R_V. (10 points)
Hence R_V can be read off as minus the intersection of the plot with vertical axis. HD 4817: 3.1, HD 11092: 3.0. (10 points)
Next, R_{r,r-i} formula and Table 14 giving R_r for HD 4817: 3.7, HD 11092: 3.6. (10 points)
Hence we take the expected values to be R_V \approx 3.1 and R_r \approx 3.7. (20 points)

parts.question:
Using the period-magnitude diagrams for 20 Cepheids from IC 342 (Figures 2 and 3) and assuming the period-luminosity relations:
〈𝑀R 〉 = −2.91 (log (𝑃/day) − 1) − 4.04 and 〈𝑀I 〉 = −3.00 (log (𝑃/day) − 1) − 4.06
where 〈𝑀R 〉 and 〈𝑀I 〉 are the mean absolute magnitudes in filters R and I, find 𝐴R for objects in IC 342. Find the distance to IC 342.
parts.reference: First let us find the apparent distance moduli \mu_{r,i} in filters r and i. Reading off the fitted values e.g. at log(P/day) = 1.6 from figures 2 and 3 and substituting into the period-luminosity relations, we find \mu_r = 29.0 mag and \mu_i = 28.6 mag , so E_{r-i} = A_r - A_i = \mu_r - \mu_i = 0.4 mag and so A_r \approx 3.7 E_{r-i} = 1.5 mag. Hence the unreddened distance modulus is \mu_0 = \mu_r - A_r = 27.5 mag and so we estimate the distance to IC 342 to be 3.2 Mpc. (20 points)
